content:
Nikhil Sharma: quick q for Runtime/SRE folks — with the KV cache compaction work landing behind a flag, does this change anything we say about customer-visible latency SLOs? (Hosted + Dedicated) Trying to line up comms for a couple Dedicated accounts that escalated on p99 spikes.

Lauren Bishop: +1. Dedicated customers are asking “are you improving the SLA / SLO numbers or just making it more stable”. We should be careful on wording.

Sean Gallagher: SRE view: we’re not changing the formal SLO targets as part of this rollout. It’s a runtime stability improvement to reduce p95/p99 spikes attributable to fragmentation. So: same SLO, better ability to *meet* it under burst/mixed-length.

Rafael Mendes: yep. We should avoid “SLO improved” language until we’ve got multiple weeks of data across pools/regions. The canary is promising but we have one model/pool where budgets need tuning.

Allison Grant: for comms: I’d frame as “tail latency stability improvements” + “reduced timeout risk under burst traffic” (esp for Dedicated). No guarantee numbers unless we attach a range with caveats + measurement method.

Nikhil Sharma: makes sense. can we share any specific claim like “p99 improved by X%” for Dedicated?

Mateo Alvarez: not broadly yet. We have internal perf suite + canary deltas, but they’re workload-dependent. Also, compaction is feature-flagged and budgets may differ by pool. If you need a customer-facing statement, safer: “targeting meaningful reduction in fragmentation-driven p99 spikes; initial canary shows improvement without median regression.”

Omar El-Sayed: adding detail: compaction reduces allocator churn + re-alloc failures, which were causing the bursty p99 cliffs. Expectation is fewer multi-second outliers, not a wholesale shift in steady-state latency. If customer asks “will my p50 be faster?” answer is probably “no material change”.

Lauren Bishop: ok. for Dedicated accounts specifically, can we say “we’ll enable this first on your pool” or is that too committal?

Sean Gallagher: we can offer “early enablement” *after* we’ve completed the one hosted region + one dedicated pool canary and we’re confident in rollback. For any named customer pool, we need a change window + explicit monitoring plan.

Rafael Mendes: +1. If it’s an escalated account, we can do a monitored enablement with runtime oncall + SRE on bridge. But we should keep the default messaging as “rolling out progressively”.

Aisha Bello: also note: if they ask about SLA credits / contractual SLO, nothing changes in terms of the written SLA for Dedicated. This is an engineering improvement to reduce risk of SLO burn.

Nikhil Sharma: got it. Proposed wording for customer update (tell me if anything is wrong):
“Over the next few weeks we’re rolling out a serving-runtime change designed to reduce tail latency spikes caused by KV-cache fragmentation under bursty workloads. This does not change the published latency SLO/SLA, but it improves stability and reduces the likelihood of p99 outliers/timeouts during traffic surges. Rollout is gradual and can be enabled per pool with monitoring and rollback.”

Allison Grant: that’s good. I’d add “no changes required on your side; no API behavior changes” to reduce worry.

Omar El-Sayed: +1. Also avoid the term “defragmentation” — it triggers questions about pauses. “Online compaction with bounded budget” is more accurate but maybe too deep; “memory compaction with guardrails to avoid latency regressions” works.

Lauren Bishop: can we give a rough timeline at least? accounts want dates.

Sean Gallagher: high level ok: “canary now / this week; broader rollout contingent on canary metrics.” Don’t promise a fixed date unless we’re pinning a pool.

Mateo Alvarez: agree. If a Dedicated account needs a date, route through Lauren + SRE and we’ll schedule after canary signoff.

Nikhil Sharma: perfect. I’ll draft a short note for the two escalated Dedicated accounts with this framing and caveats. Will sync with Lauren on whether we propose early enablement.

Lauren Bishop: thx. looping you all if/when they ask for “new SLO numbers” so we keep answers consistent.

Rafael Mendes: please do. also if they want to track it, we can share what signals we’re watching (p99, allocation failures) but keep internal thresholds internal.

Allison Grant: +1. If you want a single line for “what we’re watching”: “allocator failure rate” + “fragmentation ratio” + “p99 latency by route/model” — without numbers.

Nikhil Sharma: 👍 will do.

(Sean Gallagher reacted with :thumbsup:)

(Mateo Alvarez reacted with :white_check_mark:)
